title: Everyone's Voice Matters: Quantifying Annotation Disagreement Using Demographic Information

bias_targets.methodology: Predicting annotation disagreement by appending annotator gender identities (e.g., woman, man, transgender, non-binary) to input text for a RoBERTa model, and simulating artificial demographic combinations to evaluate variance in subjective labeling.

Incorporating annotator race and ethnicity into text prompts to train a language model on predicting annotation disagreement, and testing simulated diverse racial profiles to identify disagreement variance in subjective tasks.
Using annotator age ranges as demographic inputs to predict annotation disagreement and simulating varied age groups to evaluate their impact on subjective NLP task labels.

Appending annotator political affiliation (e.g., liberal, conservative) as demographic context to text inputs to predict label disagreement and model the subjective opinions of different political groups.

Using annotator education levels (e.g., high school, bachelor) as demographic features combined with text to predict disagreement rates and evaluate how educational background affects subjective annotations.
